literature.headline_zh: 人腺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人腺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 转基因小鼠表现出剂量依赖性体重减轻、肺组织中病毒复制强劲以及鼻内攻击后特征性组织病理学变化。疫苗接种 诱导强烈的 HAdV-55 特异性 IgG 和中和抗体反应,与对照组相比,接种疫苗的小鼠表现出显着减轻的体重减轻和加速的恢复。 [10.71150/jm.2605005]
有证据表明,HAdV-B3 感染与免疫性血小板减少症和血栓形成相关,这表明天然腺病毒感染和腺病毒 媒介 相关疾病之间存在共同的血小板因子 4 靶向免疫机制。 [10.1056/nejmc2605960]
我们在所有三个成对比较中鉴定出 106 个显示差异甲基化的基因。 [10.3390/pathogens15090988]
人们一致认为,HAdV 仍然是 HCT 后发病和 死亡率 的重要原因,特别是在 T 细胞免疫受损的患者中。已提出 HAdV 感染和疾病的国际共识定义,以提高报告临床和研究结果的一致性。越来越多的证据支持胃肠道是病毒持续存在的储存宿主,粪便病毒载量上升通常先于侵袭性感染。 [10.1097/qco.0000000000001245]
鉴定出两组 GRAd 媒介,GRAd25 在肿瘤和正常细胞中显示出广泛的复制,GRAd32 在肺癌细胞系中显示出自然选择性复制,而在正常细胞中基本上不活跃。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10623650/v1]

The evidence reports that HAdV-B3 infection is associated with immune thrombocytopenia and thrombosis, suggesting a shared platelet factor 4–targeted immune mechanism between natural adenovirus infection and adenoviral vector–associated disease. [10.1056/nejmc2605960]
We identified 106 genes showing differential methylation across all three pairwise comparisons. [10.3390/pathogens15090988]

There is a consensus that HAdV remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality following HCT, especially in patients with impaired T-cell immunity. Two groups of GRAd vectors were identified, with GRAd25 showing broad replication in both tumor and normal cells, and GRAd32 demonstrating natural selective replication in lung cancer cell lines while being largely inactive in normal cells. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10623650/v1]

papers.title: Establishment of a CD46 and desmoglein-2 expressing mouse model for human adenovirus type 55 vaccine evaluation.
papers.abstract: Human adenovirus type 55 (HAdV-55) is an emerging respiratory pathogen associated with severe pneumonia, for which no licensed vaccines are currently available. The lack of physiologically relevant small-animal models has limited preclinical evaluation of vaccine candidates. In this study, we generated a transgenic mouse model co-expressing human CD46 and desmoglein-2 (DSG-2), key entry receptors for HAdV-55, and evaluated its utility for vaccine efficacy testing. A bicistronic expression system enabling simultaneous expression of CD46 and DSG-2 was constructed and functionally validated in vitro, demonstrating enhanced susceptibility to HAdV-55 infection. The transgenic mice exhibited dose-dependent weight loss, robust viral replication in lung tissues, and characteristic histopathological changes following intranasal challenge, recapitulating key features of human adenoviral pneumonia. Using this model, we assessed the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an inactivated HAdV-55 (iHAdV-55) vaccine formulated with alum. Vaccination induced strong HAdV-55-specific IgG and neutralizing antibody responses, which increased over time following prime-boost immunization. Upon viral challenge, vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced weight loss and accelerated recovery compared to controls. Viral load analysis demonstrated effective control of viral replication and clearance in vaccinated animals. Collectively, these findings establish the CD46/DSG-2 transgenic mouse as a physiologically relevant and translationally valuable model for HAdV-55 infection and demonstrate that iHAdV-55 vaccination confers robust humoral immunity and protective efficacy. This platform provides a critical tool for the development and preclinical evaluation of adenovirus-targeted vaccines and therapeutics.

analysis_zh.methods: 构建了双顺反子表达系统以实现CD46和DSG-2的同时表达,并且该模型在体外进行了功能验证。然后使用该模型评估用明矾配制的灭活 HAdV-55 (iHAdV-55) 疫苗 的免疫原性和保护功效。
analysis_zh.main_results: 转基因小鼠表现出剂量依赖性体重减轻、肺组织中病毒复制强劲以及鼻内攻击后特征性组织病理学变化。疫苗接种 诱导强烈的 HAdV-55 特异性 IgG 和中和抗体反应,与对照组相比,接种疫苗的小鼠表现出显着减轻的体重减轻和加速的恢复。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果将 CD46/DSG-2 转基因小鼠确立为 HAdV-55 感染的生理相关且具有转化价值的模型,并证明 iHAdV-55 疫苗接种 具有强大的体液免疫和保护功效。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该平台为腺病毒靶向 疫苗 和疗法的开发和临床前评估提供了关键工具,满足了对更好的模型来评估 疫苗 候选药物针对 HAdV-55 的需求。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括使用转基因小鼠模型,该模型可能无法完全概括人类感染的所有方面。由于缺乏直接的人类验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Cross-Cohort Integration of Blood DNA Methylation and Sepsis Transcriptomes Prioritizes TP53INP1 as a Candidate Associated with B-Cell Transcriptomic Patterns in Pediatric HAdV-7-Associated Sepsis
papers.abstract: Human adenovirus type 7 (HAdV-7) can cause severe pneumonia and sepsis in children, but the associated host epigenetic and immune alterations remain poorly defined. We profiled peripheral-blood DNA methylation in 11 children with HAdV-7-associated sepsis (6 survivors and 5 non-survivors) and 5 pediatric controls without clinically detectable HAdV-7 infection using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing. Differentially methylated genes were integrated with pediatric septic shock transcriptomic modules from GSE26440, and their cellular distribution and predicted regulatory effects were explored using the single-cell dataset GSE167363 and scTenifoldKnk. We identified 106 genes showing differential methylation across all three pairwise comparisons. Cross-cohort integration prioritized 19 candidate genes, among which TP53INP1 showed preferential expression in B cells in the external sepsis single-cell dataset. In silico perturbation of TP53INP1 was associated with changes in interferon-stimulated and antiviral genes, including TRIM22, IFI44L, and PARP14. These findings identify TP53INP1 as a hypothesis-generating candidate linking HAdV-7-associated whole-blood methylation changes with B-cell regulatory networks observed in an external sepsis dataset. Given the small discovery cohort and absence of experimental validation, the findings are exploratory and require confirmation in independent cohorts.

papers.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review recent advances in the epidemiology, diagnosis, and management of human adenovirus (HAdV) infection following haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) and other cellular therapies, with emphasis on risk stratification, molecular surveillance, and emerging therapies. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies have improved understanding of the interplay between viral burden, immune reconstitution, and progression to invasive HAdV disease following HCT. International consensus definitions of HAdV infection and disease have recently been proposed and may improve consistency in the reporting of clinical and research outcomes. Increasing evidence supports the gastrointestinal tract as a reservoir for viral persistence, with rising stool viral loads often preceding invasive infection. Intravenous brincidofovir has emerged as a promising alternative to cidofovir, demonstrating preliminary antiviral activity without the nephrotoxicity associated with cidofovir or the gastrointestinal toxicity observed with oral brincidofovir. HAdV-specific cytotoxic T-lymphocyte therapies have also shown encouraging efficacy in refractory infection. SUMMARY: HAdV remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality following HCT, particularly in patients with impaired T-cell immunity. Key challenges include optimal surveillance strategies, treatment thresholds, and management of high-risk patients. Advances in molecular diagnostics, standardized disease definitions, brincidofovir, and virus-specific T-cell therapies may facilitate higher quality clinical research and support more standardized, evidence-based approaches to HAdV management.

papers.title: A novel Gorilla-derived oncolytic Adenovirus with natural selective replication in lung cancer cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Oncolytic virotherapy uses viruses to selectively infect and destroy cancer cells while sparing normal tissues and represents a promising approach for cancer treatment. Most adenoviral platforms currently under development are derived from human adenovirus type 5, motivating the search for alternative vectors with distinct biological properties. Here, we investigated gorilla-derived adenoviruses (GRAd) as candidate oncolytic platforms. We identified two groups of GRAd vectors with markedly different biological behaviors. GRAd25 displayed broad replication in both tumor and normal cells, whereas GRAd32 showed a naturally restricted replication profile, efficiently replicating in selected lung cancer cell lines while remaining largely inactive in normal cells. To broaden tumor cell targeting while preserving this selectivity, we generated a chimeric virus, GRAd32Fk25, by replacing the native GRAd32 fiber knob with that of GRAd25. The resulting vector exhibited enhanced infectivity and improved oncolytic activity in multiple cancer cell lines while maintaining restricted replication in normal cells. We further engineered GRAd32Fk25 to express EV20, an anti-HER3 therapeutic antibody, and demonstrated production of a functional molecule capable of binding HER3 and inhibiting downstream signaling. These findings establish gorilla-derived adenoviruses as a versatile platform for the development of tumor-selective oncolytic therapies.

papers.title: Development and angiographic utilization of the Oncopig liver cancer model: a comprehensive pictorial review
papers.abstract: Image-guided locoregional therapies are central to the management of liver cancer.Large-animal models are valuable preclinical tools for advancing interventional oncology because they allow testing with standard clinical imaging platforms and devices.The Oncopig TM is a genetically engineered porcine model that enables site-specific tumor formation through inducible expression of KRAS G12D and TP53 R167H following exposure to Cre recombinase.This pictorial essay illustrates the technical methodology for liver tumor induction in Oncopigs and demonstrates the angiographic use of tumor-bearing animals for evaluation of transarterial therapies.Liver tumors were induced using an ex vivo transgene activation approach in which liver biopsy specimens were incubated with an adenoviral vector expressing Cre recombinase and injected percutaneously into the liver under ultrasound guidance.Tumor development occurred in 34/37 (92%) induction sites across 17 Oncopigs and was confirmed by contrast-enhanced computed tomography.Hepatic arteriography using standard clinical devices enabled selective catheterization of tumor-feeding arteries.This pictorial essay provides a technical guide for investigators studying liver-directed therapies in a translational large-animal model.

Tumor development was confirmed in 92% of induction sites across 17 animals, and hepatic arteriography was demonstrated as a method for selective catheterization of tumor-feeding arteries. The study provides a technical guide for using this model in translational research, highlighting its potential for advancing interventional oncology. However, the findings are limited to a preclinical model and do not extend to human clinical outcomes, resulting in moderate evidence strength.
